newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real falls ahead of Carnival holiday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real falls ahead of Carnival holiday.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.07 percent to close at 1.0468 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market as banks held dollars in anticipation of a mini-devaluation later in the week, dealers said.
"February is a short month and next week is carnival. So we are expecting the Central Bank to set a mini-devalution by the end of this week," one dealer said.

Market players said the Central Bank would probably lower the mini-band by 0.05 percent to 0.10 percent by the end of the week. Tuesday, the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.0460 to 1.0510 reais.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Wednesday surplus of $188 million.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.01 percent to end at 1.0518, according to dealers.
In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.28 percent to end at 1.082.
